content: We are going to make the Deku Shield from The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Image 1). Under [k]Render > Color Management[/k] set [k]View > Standard[/k] for a less filmic look (Image 2) and set [k]View Layer > Passes > Data > Depth[/k] enabled for the Grease Pencil later (Image 3). Add a cube and scale it down in the y-axis (Image 4). From the front add a [k]Loop Cut[/k] and give it a general shield shape (Image 5). Add a few more cuts and to make it match the game (Image 6). Come around to the top and angle it out (Image 7).

image.caption: Image 1 - Making the Deku Shield from The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
Image 2 - Going to Render > Color Management and setting View > Standard for a less filmic look
Image 3 - Enabling View Layer > Passes > Data > Depth for the Grease Pencil later
Image 4 - Adding a cube and scaling it down in the y-axis
Image 5 - Adding a Loop Cut from the front and giving it a general shield shape
Image 6 - Adding a few more cuts to match the game
Image 7 - Coming around to the top and angling it out

content: Add some more [k]Loop Cuts[/k] across and up and down (Image 8). [k]2[/k] into [k]Edge Mode[/k] and select all interior edges except the middle one (Image 9). [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to bevel them with two segments (Image 10). Set [k]Transform Pivot Point > Individual Origins[/k] and [k]S[/k] all the inner edges to create the appearance of wooden slats (Image 11). Add five [k]Loop Cuts[/k] across the top and bottom sections to be used for the (Image 12). in [k]Object Mode[/k] [k]RMB > Shade Smooth[/k] and review the model (Image 13).

image.caption: Image 8 - Adding more Loop Cuts across and up and down
Image 9 - Pressing 2 to enter Edge Mode and selecting all interior edges except the middle one
Image 10 - Pressing Ctrl-B to bevel the edges with two segments
Image 11 - Setting Transform Pivot Point > Individual Origins and pressing S to scale all the inner edges to create the appearance of wooden slats
Image 12 - Adding five Loop Cuts across the top and bottom sections
Image 13 - In Object Mode, pressing RMB > Shade Smooth and reviewing the model

content: Add a cylinder with 8 vertices, rotate it 90 degrees in the x-axis and shrink it down (Image 14). [k]I[/k] to inset the face on one end, [k]G[/k] to bring it out, then [k]E[/k] to extrude it and [k]Ctrl-RMB[/k] to keep extruding sections until you get to the last one and [k]S,Z,0[/k] to flatten it (Image 15). Set the handle's origin to the world origin and add a [k]Mirror Modifier[/k] (Image 16). Since this is the handle to fit a hand you might want to move the parts closer together (Image 17). Enable [k]Clipping[/k] in the [k]Mirror Modifier[/k] and extrude the bottom face down (Image 18). Move the handle over to the side where the wielder would naturally carry it (Image 19).

image.caption: Image 14 - Adding a cylinder with 8 vertices, rotating it 90 degrees in the x-axis and shrinking it down
Image 15 - Pressing I to inset the face on one end, G to bring it out, E to extrude and Ctrl-RMB to keep extruding sections, then pressing S, Z, 0 on the last one to flatten it
Image 16 - Setting the handle's origin to the world origin and adding a Mirror Modifier
Image 17 - Moving the parts of the handle closer together to fit a hand
Image 18 - Enabling Clipping in the Mirror Modifier and extruding the bottom face down
Image 19 - Moving the handle over to the side where the wielder would naturally carry it

content: Add a cube and scale it down (Image 20). Use [k]E[/k] and [k]Ctrl-RMB[/k] to extrude the strap shape (Image 21). Add a [k]Mirror Modifier[/k] with [k]Clipping[/k] and complete the loop (Image 22). Add a [k]Subdivision Surface Modifier[/k] for a smoother look (Image 23). Position the strap (Image 24).

image.caption: Image 20 - Adding a cube and scaling it down
Image 21 - Using E and Ctrl-RMB to extrude the strap shape
Image 22 - Adding a Mirror Modifier with Clipping and completing the loop
Image 23 - Adding a Subdivision Surface Modifier for a smoother look
Image 24 - Positioning the strap

content: Select the shield geometry and add a [k]Displace Modifier[/k] with a new Texture and name it 'LumpyWood' (Image 25). Open the [k]Texture Properties[/k] and set [k]Type > Voronoi[/k] (Image 26). Adjust [k]Colors > Contrast[/k] and [k]Voronoi > Size[/k] until you get the result you want (Image 27).

image.caption: Image 25 - Selecting the shield geometry and adding a Displace Modifier with a new Texture named 'LumpyWood'
Image 26 - Opening the Texture Properties and setting Type > Voronoi
Image 27 - Adjusting Colors > Contrast and Voronoi > Size until getting the desired result

content: Open the [k]Shading Workspace[/k] and in the shield's shade network add a [k]Shader to RGB[/k] and [k]Color Ramp[/k](Image 28). Give the [k]Color Ramp[/k] five stops (Image 29) :

image.caption: Image 28 - Opening the Shading Workspace and adding a Shader to RGB and Color Ramp to the shield's shade network
Image 29 - Giving the Color Ramp five stops

content: Set up shader networks for the handle and strap as well: (Image 30).

image.caption: Image 30 - Setting up shader networks for the handle and strap as well

content: Add a second material to the shield named 'shieldBorder'; change its [k]Surface[/k] to [k]Emission[/k] and set the [k]Color[/k] to #331A20 (Image 31). Add a [k]Solidify Modifier[/k] and set [k]Normals > Flip[/k] enabled and [k]Materials > Material Offset[/k] to 1 so it uses the second material slot (Image 32). Under [k]Material Properties[/k] for the second material, enable [k]Settings > Surface > Backface Culling > Camera[/k] (Image 33). Adjust the [k]Solidify Modifier > Thickness[/k] setting to see thicken the shield border (you should disable the [k]Face Orientation[/k] overlay if you have it enabled) (Image 34).

image.caption: Image 31 - Adding a second material to the shield named 'shieldBorder', changing its Surface to Emission and setting the Color to #331A20
Image 32 - Adding a Solidify Modifier, enabling Normals > Flip and setting Materials > Material Offset to 1 so it uses the second material slot
Image 33 - Enabling Settings > Surface > Backface Culling > Camera under Material Properties for the second material
Image 34 - Adjusting the Solidify Modifier > Thickness setting to thicken the shield border, with the Face Orientation overlay disabled
